pages.q: Is Tigard, Oregon a good place to live if you rent?
pages.short: For a lot of renters, yes. Tigard sits in the Portland metro next to Interstate 5 and Highway 217, so getting to Portland, Beaverton and Lake Oswego is easy. You also get Washington Square mall close by, plus newer apartment communities like Montage in the Tigard Triangle.

p: Tigard is a Portland suburb that works well when you split your week between the city and the west side. Interstate 5 runs along the city's eastern edge and Highway 217 links I 5 to US 26 in the north, so most of the metro is a straightforward drive.

Everyday errands are close. Washington Square has about 210 shops and restaurants plus a food court, anchored by Macy's, Nordstrom, JCPenney and an Apple Store. Bridgeport Village, another big shopping and dining stop, sits off I 5.

sections.h: Getting around without a long drive
p: Tigard is close to Portland without being in the middle of it. One mapping estimate puts the drive at about 11 miles and about 20 minutes, and rush hour takes longer. TriMet Route 12 runs between Tigard and downtown Portland along Pacific Highway and Barbur Boulevard, and Washington Square Transit Center is served by five bus lines.

Montage is a new apartment community at 13155 SW 68th Parkway in the Tigard Triangle, about 1 mile from Washington Square, with direct access to Hwy 217 and I 5. Bridgeport Village is about 10 minutes away and Lake Oswego about 15.

Inside, homes have 10 foot ceilings, quartz counters, stainless steel appliances and a full size washer and dryer. On site there is a pool and spa, sky lounge, fitness center, coworking spaces and a game room with a golf simulator.

Map your real commute at the hours you would drive it, walk the area around Washington Square on a weekend, and tour a few homes. For current Montage rents and specials, see the Montage roommate guide page, then call the leasing team at 971 399 3242.

Beaverton is a natural fit when most of your trips head north toward US 26. Tigard makes sense when you also head south on I 5 toward Lake Oswego, Tualatin or Wilsonville, or into Portland.

Nike's world headquarters is on a 286 acre campus in unincorporated Washington County near Beaverton. Montage's guide page lists easy reach of Nike HQ, and Hwy 217 is the main link between Tigard and Beaverton.

pages.q: What is a lease up apartment community, and is it a good time to rent?
pages.short: A lease up community is a newly built apartment property that is filling its homes for the first time. Because the building is new, renters often get first pick of floor plans and views, brand new finishes, and sometimes move in specials. Montage in Tigard is a new community, and its guide page lists the latest offers.

p: When a new building opens, its homes start out empty. The lease up period is the stretch of time when the leasing team works to fill them. During that time you will often see newer appliances and finishes, hallways and common areas that have not seen years of wear, and amenities that were just finished.
Lease up communities also tend to use move in specials to attract their first residents. The details vary by building and by floor plan, and they can change week to week.

pages.q: How much can an apartment charge for an application fee in Oregon?
pages.short: In Oregon, a landlord can charge an application or screening fee only to cover the actual average cost of screening you. They must give you their written screening criteria and a receipt for the fee. Only one screening fee can be charged in a 60 day period, and the fee must be refunded in some cases.

p: The Oregon Legislature's own renter and landlord guide sums up the screening fee rules this way:
bullets: The fee can only cover the actual average cost of screening an applicant
The landlord must adopt written screening criteria and give them to applicants
You must get a receipt for any screening fee
Only one screening fee can be charged within a 60 day period
No fee can be collected when no units will be available within a reasonable time
The fee must be refunded in some cases, such as when the unit is rented before your application is screened

sections.h: Other things you should be told
p: During the application process, the landlord must also tell you whether renter's liability insurance is required. If a landlord does not follow the screening fee rules, Oregon law gives applicants a way to recover money, so keep your receipt and any written criteria you were given.
This is general information, not legal advice. Laws change, so check the current rules or ask a local attorney or legal aid office about your situation.

Before you apply anywhere, ask for the screening criteria in writing and read the income and credit requirements, so you only pay to apply where you are likely to qualify. If you are applying with a roommate, ask how each person is screened.

For Montage, the leasing team can walk you through the criteria and current fees. Call 971 399 3242, Monday to Friday 9 AM to 6 PM or weekends 10 AM to 5 PM. Current rents and specials are on the Montage roommate guide page.

Gather recent proof of income, a photo ID and contact details for past landlords before you apply, so screening moves quickly. If anything on your record needs context, ask the leasing team how to share it. Having everything ready also helps you move faster once you find a home you like.

pages.q: When do you get your security deposit back in Oregon?
pages.short: Oregon gives a landlord 31 days after your rental agreement ends to refund your deposit and any prepaid rent owed. If they keep part of it, they must give you a written accounting that lists the amount and reason for each deduction.

p: According to the Oregon Legislature's renter and landlord guide, a landlord has 31 days after the rental agreement ends to refund all deposits and prepaid rent owed. Instead of a full refund, the landlord can send a written accounting that itemizes the amount and purpose of each deduction.
If a landlord fails to give the required accounting, or withholds money in bad faith, a tenant may be able to recover twice the amount wrongfully withheld.

bullets: During the first year, a landlord generally cannot require a new or larger security deposit, with limited exceptions such as when you add a pet
After the first year, an added deposit must come with at least three months to pay it
A landlord may only charge fees allowed by law and described in your written rental agreement

p: Take dated photos of every room on move in day and again when you move out. Keep a copy of your lease, report anything broken in writing, and give the landlord your forwarding address when you leave.

At Montage, ask the leasing team which deposits apply to your home, and whether your pet deposit is refundable (the guide page says it is). Call 971 399 3242, or see the Montage roommate guide page for current pricing.

A deposit is money held and returned, minus allowed deductions, after you move out. A fee is a charge you do not get back. Oregon law limits landlords to fees that are allowed by law and described in your written rental agreement, and a landlord may not charge a fee at the start of a tenancy for expected landlord expenses. Read your lease so you know which charges are which.
This is general information, not legal advice. Laws change, so check the current rules or ask a local attorney or legal aid office about your situation.

pages.q: Can a landlord raise your rent during the first year of a lease in Oregon?
pages.short: Generally, no. Under Oregon law a landlord may not increase rent during the first year of a tenancy, except for week to week rentals. After the first year, rent can usually go up once in any 12 month period, and most tenancies require at least 90 days of written notice first.

p: The Oregon Legislature's renter and landlord guide lists these rent increase rules:
bullets: No rent increase during the first year of a tenancy, except week to week tenancies
After the first year, rent can generally go up once in any 12 month period
Most tenancies need at least 90 days of written notice before an increase
Week to week tenancies need at least seven days of notice

sections.h: Ending a month to month lease
p: If your lease turns month to month, Oregon lets a tenant end it by giving the landlord at least 30 days of written notice. Read your lease for any terms about ending a fixed term lease early, since those are set by the agreement.
This is general information, not legal advice. Laws change, so check the current rules or ask a local attorney or legal aid office about your situation.

sections.h: Questions to ask before you sign
p: Ask how renewals work, when you will hear about your renewal rate, and whether longer lease terms are offered. Also ask about required monthly fees, since your total monthly cost is more than base rent.

At Montage, the leasing team can explain lease lengths and renewals. Call 971 399 3242, Monday to Friday 9 AM to 6 PM or weekends 10 AM to 5 PM. Current rents and specials are on the Montage roommate guide page.

Rent rules only cover part of what you pay. Before you sign, add up base rent, required monthly fees, parking, pet rent if you have a pet, utilities and renter's insurance if it is required. Knowing your full number now makes renewal time less of a surprise, and it lets you compare communities fairly, including any move in specials that lower your cost at the start.
